title: AutoCount migration effective import-time field-routing evidence (v1)
description: External input contract for the effective import-time field-routing state that applies to one import operation, under final design lock DL-XB-140-001-A4. Repository tooling MUST NOT inspect live AutoCount settings; an operator or a later separately authorised lane observes the actual import-time configuration and records it here, and the repository only validates the document. Recognised headers do not prove routing: any import-time configuration capable of changing source-header to AutoCount-destination routing is contract authority. Absence of this document is never 'disabled' - it is UNKNOWN and NOT IMPORT READY. A previously saved mapping is not standing authority, which is why the evidence is bound to a single import_operation_id. Workbook shape, a New/Update preview, row counts, amount totals and a previous successful import are not routing proof and have no representation here. Contains no credentials and no private business rows.

schema_version.description: Fixed contract version. An unrecognised value is refused fail-closed.

import_operation_id.description: Must equal the manifest import_operation_id. A different value means the observation belongs to another import operation, so it is treated as not current and blocks with UNKNOWN rather than being reused as standing authority.

state.description: Exactly one recorded effective routing state. 'enabled' requires a complete mapping that binds every declared qualified source identity to the qualified destination the contract declares; a partial mapping blocks UNKNOWN and a differing destination blocks MISMATCH. 'disabled' and 'unavailable_not_applicable' are POSITIVE observations that satisfy this gate on their own. 'UNKNOWN' blocks. There is no implicit fourth reading: not supplying the document at all is also UNKNOWN.

observation_ref.description: Non-secret reference to how the state was observed (for example an operator evidence note identifier). Required for every state other than UNKNOWN, so a positive 'disabled' claim always carries provenance.

mappings.description: The effective source-to-destination binding observed when state is 'enabled'. Both sides are contract-qualified identities: a bare field name never becomes a routing identity merely because its spelling matches. A binding for a source outside the declared contract blocks MISMATCH. Exactly one unambiguous effective binding may be recorded per qualified identity: a repeated source is refused whether the destinations agree or conflict, and a destination claimed by two distinct sources is refused as non-bijective. JSON Schema cannot express that - two objects sharing a source but differing in destination are not duplicates under JSON equality, so uniqueItems would not catch them - therefore the validating implementation enforces it, which is what stops the array order deciding the verdict.
